The present application is filed seeking pre-arrest bail in FIR No. 170/2025 dated 08.04.2025,
registered at Police Station Paschim Vihar West for offences under Sections 420/406/467/468/471/120B/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
2.

The FIR was registered on a complaint given by one person, namely, Parminder Singh, who alleged to have invested a sum of 10,00,000/- with the accused persons including the applicant in the form of bank transfer, crypto currency transfer and cash with a promise of huge returns.
It is alleged that the complainant made the investments in the year 2021 and has not received any amount till date.

sentences.text: The learned Senior counsel for the applicant submits that a frivolous complaint has been filed which led to the registration of the FIR.
He submits that even though the complainant has alleged to have invested a sum of 10,00,000/-, however, no proof of such deposit has been given.
4. He submits that the co-accused, Ravi Shankar, who is alleged to have a similar role, has already been admitted on bail by this Court and chargesheet has also been filed by the police.
He submits that no purpose would be served by subjecting the applicant to custodial interrogation.

5. He lastly submits that even as per the case of the prosecution as stated in the status report filed before the learned Trial Court, only a sum of 10,00,000/- has allegedly been received by the applicant.

He submits that without prejudice to the fact that no proof of such deposit has been given,
the applicant is willing to deposit the said amount in order to show his bona fide.
6. Ms. Nandita Rao, learned Senior counsel appears on behalf of the complainant and states that multiple people have been cheated and that she represents all the victims.
7. She vehemently opposes the grant of any relief to the applicant and states that multiple victims have been cheated of their hard-earned monies.

8. The learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the State submits that process under Section 82 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 has already been initiated against the applicant and, in such circumstances, the applicant is not entitled to grant of any relief.

9. Issue notice.
10. Let status report be filed within a period of two weeks.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 08/09/2025 at 23:24:56 11.

The status report filed before the learned Trial Court mentions the details of investment made by ten persons and the Police has also mentioned the total cheated amount against each complainant in the chart which indicates that a sum of 10,00,000/- has allegedly been transferred in the account of the applicant.
12. The applicant claims that no such amount was ever transferred and no date for such transfer has also been provided.
13. Undisputedly, when the applicant is evading the process of law, pre-arrest bail, which is an extraordinary remedy, ought not to be exercised in the aid of such accused person.

sentences.text: However, in the present case, as noted above, the co- accused - Ravi Shankar who is alleged to have a similar role, has already been admitted on bail.

15. Even though it is now claimed that there are multiple victims, it is relevant to note that the chargesheet has already been filed in regard to the complaint made by the complainant - Parminder Singh.
The status report filed before the learned Trial Court also indicates that the amount received by the applicant through bank transfer is approximately 10,00,000/-.

16. Considering the above, the State is directed not to arrest the applicant till the next date of hearing on the applicant depositing a sum of 10,00,000/- within a period of two weeks with the Registrar General of this Court.
17. Updated status report be filed before the next date of hearing.

18. List on 28.10.2025.
AMIT MAHAJAN, J SEPTEMBER 8, 2025/"SS"
